We develop a spherical rigorous coupled-wave method that incorporates the spatially dependent anisotropic magnetic permeability associated with the vortex texture. papers.abs: The topological charge of a bound state in the continuum (BIC) can flip when the BIC merges with other polarization singularities or, as recently shown, at band flips. Here, using a coupled-mode analysis, we derive an analytical expression for the topological charge of symmetry-protected BICs in one-dimensional single-layer photonic lattices. In vertically symmetric lattices, each charge flip occurs simultaneously in the upward and downward radiation channels. papers.abs: Boundary dissipation can reshape the spatial profiles and decay properties of topological edge modes in Chern insulators. papers.abs: Field applications in chemical sensing, from portable safety monitors to mobile robots, require models that are lightweight, fast to respond, and can be recalibrated from limited labelled data. papers.title: Bright Solitons in Non-Hermitian systems: Exploring the interplay of $\mathcal{PT}$ Symmetry and Wadati Structure
papers.abs: In this study, we revisit the subject of optical solitons in non-Hermitian potentials. For the underlying model of the focusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation with a complex localized potential, we offer a classification of such models into four canonical cases. These correspond to (a) $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Wadati potentials, (b) $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Wadati potentials, (c) Non-$\mathcal{PT}$ but Wadati potentials, and (d) complex potentials with neither $\mathcal{PT}$ nor Wadati symmetries. We study the existence and stability of optical solitons across prototypical model variations spanning all four relevant quadrants. We complement such an investigation with a low-dimensional effective description based on a non-conservative variational approximation method. The variational framework is assessed in terms of its ability to represent the structural properties and bifurcations of solutions. {Our results suggest that continuous families of bright solitons persist across sectors (a)--(c). papers.title: In-situ Control of the Photon-Magnon Synchronized Mode in a Miniaturized Magnetometer
papers.abs: Photon-magnon synchronized modes (PMSMs) provide a route for magnetic-field sensing by exploiting their enhanced field responsivity due to cusp points (CPs). However, the previous PMSM magnetometer relies on bulky discrete components and lacks in situ control of photon-magnon interactions, limiting its integration and adaptability. Here, we demonstrate a miniaturized PMSM magnetometer integrated on a printed circuit board. A variable resistor is used to tune the photon-magnon coupling strength in situ. By adjusting the variable resistor, the electromagnetic boundary condition of the magnetometer is altered; hence, the reservoir-mediated photon-magnon interaction is changed. The coupling strength shows a non-monotonic dependence on the reflection coefficient adjusted by the variable resistor and reaches its minimum at the impedance matching condition. Furthermore, we develop a non-Hermitian model with standing-wave interference to describe the PMSM dispersion and derive the critical condition for CP formation. papers.title: Diagnostic-dependent lasting Mpemba effect in a parametrically driven oscillator
papers.abs: For two Gaussian preparations of a detuned degenerate parametric amplifier below threshold, the trace distance shows a lasting Mpemba reversal, whereas the relative entropy eventually restores the initial order and the Hilbert--Schmidt distance alternates indefinitely. All three diagnostics agree on the initial order, and these orders persist on open sets of preparations and quadratic generators. The disagreement is possible because a real relaxation mode and a complex-conjugate pair share the leading decay rate, a coincidence that holds for any single-mode quadratic oscillator with linear damping in the elliptic regime. Number symmetry hides their competition in the undriven trace-distance tail, and parametric driving exposes it. Near a pure stationary state, the relative entropy strongly weights changes of the symplectic eigenvalue, which approximately follow the nonoscillating energy deviation; thermal occupation weakens this preference. papers.title: Spectral Oscillations and Temporal Meandering of Dissipative Solitons in a Moving Intracavity Phase Potential
papers.abs: Dissipative solitons (DSs) provide a prototypical platform for studying nonequilibrium dynamics governed by the interplay between nonlinearity, dissipation, and external driving. In particular, subjected to external potentials, DSs exhibit a rich variety of nonlinear dynamical behaviors. This work investigates DS dynamics in a moving intracavity potential generated by phase modulation whose frequency is detuned from an integer multiple of the cavity repetition rate. Modulation detuning introduces a timescale mismatch between the DS and the moving potential, leading to two distinct dynamical regimes. At large detuning, the DS cannot continuously track the moving potential and exhibits persistent spectral oscillations and temporal meandering, whereas at sufficiently small detuning it enters a synchronized locking state. Furthermore, both the oscillation period and amplitude can be tuned via the modulation detuning and modulation depth. papers.title: Optically gated transduction enables silicon electrical readout of mid-infrared light
papers.abs: Silicon is the dominant platform for integrated photonics, yet its wide electronic bandgap of 1.1 eV fundamentally prevents efficient detection of mid-infrared (MIR) photons through direct valence band to conduction band excitation. Existing approaches therefore seek to enhance sub-bandgap absorption or introduce external infrared absorbers. Here we demonstrate a profoundly different detection strategy based on optically gated transduction, in which MIR photons modulate a pre-established excitation state rather than directly generating photocarriers. Our device integrates Nd3+-doped lanthanide nanoparticles with an inverse-designed Al/p-Si metasurface supporting dual resonances that simultaneously enhances optical gating in the near infrared and resonantly couples incident MIR radiation. The MIR illumination redistributes the Nd3+ emission pathways, producing an optical-state change that is converted into an electrical signal through a silicon Schottky junction. papers.title: Finite-temperature Quantum Quasinormal Mode Theory for Spatiotemporally-resolved Dissipative Cavity Quantum Magnonics
papers.abs: Cavity quantum magnonics has ushered in an unprecedented era of hybrid light-matter interfaces in which microwave photons, collective spin excitations, and superconducting or spin qubits can be coupled within a single device architecture, facilitating a versatile platform for quantum information processing. Realizing their full potential, however, requires a theory that can treat non-reciprocal magnetic media, material dissipation and open-cavity radiation losses, as well as finite-temperature fluctuations rigorously and without significant approximation. The dissipative magnonic resonances of such systems are described as quasinormal modes (QNMs), yet a consistent quantization procedure for lossy gyrotropic resonators has remained elusive. In this work, we present a finite-temperature quantum QNM theory, based on macroscopic quantum electrodynamics for non-reciprocal media and complex coordinate transformations, that achieves QNM quantization for a wide class of spatially inhomogeneous, dissipative and dispersive, cavity magnonic systems. papers.title: High-Efficiency Graphene Oxide Moiré Lenses Enabled by Cyclic Self-Assembly and Laser Nanoprinting
papers.abs: Compact optical systems with continuously tunable focal lengths are highly desirable for machine vision, biomedical imaging, and miniaturized cameras. Rotational Moiré lenses offer a planar approach to focal-length tuning, but metasurface-based implementations typically require complex nanofabrication processes that complicate large-area production. Here, we present a cyclic, mask-free fabrication strategy that combines layer-by-layer self-assembly of two-dimensional graphene oxide (GO) and poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA) with femtosecond laser nanoprinting. Repeated GO-PDDA assembly and spatially selective ablation enable atomic-scale thickness control and the construction of precise multilevel phase profiles, reducing phase-quantization errors and improving focusing efficiency. The measured focusing efficiencies of individual GO lenses increase from 22.4% for two phase levels to 54.8% for six levels. papers.title: Generation of quantum light with tunable Wigner negativity with a semiconductor quantum dot
papers.abs: Wigner-negative states of light are key resources for quantum advantage in continuous-variable optical quantum computing. They can be produced probabilistically via frequency conversion and photon detection, or deterministically by exploiting the single-photon nonlinearity of a quantum emitter. Here, we generate such Wigner-negative states of light with a tunable negativity using a single semiconductor quantum dot in a cavity. Optical coherent control of the quantum-dot transition allows to generate a quantum superposition of zero and one photon. The generated quantum states are characterized point-by-point in the phase space through homodyne measurement. The emergence of Wigner-function negativity is observed as the excitation power is increased. After correcting for collection and propagation losses, we obtain fidelities to the ideal state and quantum purities above 95%, together with near-optimal quadrature squeezing. papers.title: Ultrafast light-electron modulation for free-electron quantum optics: fundamentals and applications
papers.abs: Coherent optical modulation of free-electron wavepackets offers a route to ultrafast beam steering, energy exchange, temporal compression, and quantum-state shaping. Recent advances in photon-induced near-field electron microscopy (PINEM), ultrafast Kapitza-Dirac effect (KDE) and dielectric laser acceleration (DLA) have demonstrated strong light-electron coupling, but longitudinal energy modulation, transverse momentum transfer, and wavepacket-dependent diffraction are still commonly described with separate models. Here, we develop a unified Light-Electron Modulation (LEM) framework that treats optical near fields as programmable phase modulators for free-electron wavepackets. Within this framework, we identify longitudinal and transverse modulation channels, analogous to electro-optic phase modulation and acousto-optic diffraction of light, respectively, and show how their operation depends on wavepacket extent, recoil, phase matching, and optical-field geometry. papers.title: Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling for efficient quantum trajectories in metastable open quantum systems
papers.abs: Open quantum systems can display metastability, with multiple long-lived states coexisting. Examples include the bistability of bright and dim manifolds in nonlinear driven resonators, or the long-lived coherent states of opposite phases in parametrically-driven systems, the building block of cat-state-based quantum computers. Metastability often emerges at system sizes where density-matrix evolution is impractical. Quantum trajectories mitigate this issue by evolving wavefunctions rather than density matrices. Metastable states then emerge as attractors towards which the system rapidly relaxes until a rare switching event brings it to another attractor. Simulating them remains costly, as one must resolve fast intra-attractor dynamics over timescales long enough to gather switching statistics. To tackle this problem, we introduce the Diagonal, Switching, and Locally Optimal Unraveling (DiSLOU) method, which combines three optimization layers: (i) Switching among locally optimal unravelings that minimize the number of quantum jumps in each metastable region. papers.abs: High-refractive-index nanowires are of interest for signal enhancement in fluorescence-based biosensing. Here, through electromagnetic modelling, we demonstrate substantial fluorescence signal enhancement by incorporating a tapered section into a cylindrical nanowire and investigate two complementary tapering configurations to address practical implementation challenges. Under near-normal excitation, the excitation enhancement increases approximately linearly with taper length, reaching more than three times that of the corresponding non-tapered nanowire at a taper length of 8000 nm. In a non-imaging signal detection scheme using a low numerical aperture (NA), the proposed tapered nanowire achieves more than three orders of magnitude enhancement in fluorescence signal compared with a planar biosensor. Thus, the tapered nanowire should enable efficient fluorescence detection using compact, low-NA optical configuration. papers.abs: Quantum batteries are quantum systems that potentially serve as fuel for other quantum devices by receiving and supplying energy. In this work, we propose a theoretical scheme to enhance ergotropy and charging power of quantum Battery in the system under consideration through squeezed light. Moreover, The system comprises a coherently driven charger cavity, a strongly dissipative auxiliary cavity acting as a mediator, and an energy--storage battery cavity. Quantum nonreciprocity and directional energy flow are established via destructive quantum interference between the direct coupling path and the loss--engineered indirect path. A degenerate optical parametric amplifier integrated into the charger cavity acts as an active, phase--sensitive energy source that injects two--photon quantum excitations and anomalous correlations. Using a strictly open--quantum--system framework derived directly from the Lindblad master equation, we obtain the full expectation--value dynamics and stationary states. papers.title: Theoretical description of high-harmonic spectroscopy for uniaxial nematic and isotropic liquid crystals
papers.abs: Enabled by their controllable optical anisotropy, liquid crystals form a cornerstone of linear optical and display technologies. Bringing the versatile platform into the nonlinear regime, we explore its nonlinear optical anisotropy by high-order harmonic generation spectroscopy. Through a comprehensive study targeting gas, liquid, nematic, and crystalline phases, we present a semi-empirical tight-binding approach that provides insight into the intermolecular character of ultrafast light-driven electron dynamics across soft-matter mesophases. We demonstrate how intermolecular electron hybridization enables spectroscopic access to structural properties, such as the nematic director and order parameter. Outlining such foundational mechanisms opens avenues towards nonlinear liquid crystal devices and ultrafast soft-matter spectroscopies.

papers.title: Plasma and light: Shaping High Harmonic Generation in Time-Varying Media
papers.abs: High harmonic generation in solids is typically described under the assumption of a stationary medium. This assumption is rarely questioned because the electronic properties of most media evolve on timescales much slower than the harmonic emission process itself. However, in strongly driven time-varying transparent conductive oxides the plasma frequency, carrier density, and effective mass can evolve on the same femtosecond timescale as harmonic generation. Under these conditions, harmonic generation and material evolution are no longer independent processes. Within this context, we consider a two-field pumping scheme in which a strong field generates a comb of high-order harmonics across a broad spectral window, while a weaker field simultaneously reshapes its own individual spectral lines. Distinct from geometry-dependent wave-mixing processes, the evolving electron plasma reshapes multiple collinear harmonic channels simultaneously. papers.abs: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) has increased the demand for energy-efficient hardware, and optical computing has emerged as a promising alternative to conventional electronic processors owing to its high parallelism and potentially lower power consumption. Numerical results demonstrate that the reservoir mirror reflectance, the size of the encoded figure, and the refractive-index contrast between the reservoir and the encoded figure modify the nonlinearity of the system, as verified via pairwise similarity estimates. papers.title: XL MIMO Extreme Learning Machines: Wave-Domain Inference with Stacked Metasurfaces
papers.abs: The recently envisioned goal-oriented communications paradigm requires machine learning inference to be performed directly on wirelessly transferred data, by splitting neural network computations between the transmitter, the Receiver (RX), and the wireless channel. Such approaches aim to offload large portions of the computation onto the channel itself, which is often controlled by reconfigurable MetaSurfaces (MSs). Typical MS-parametrized systems, however, enable only limited computation offloading in the wave domain, usually corresponding to a single neural network layer, due to adverse channel fading effects and the almost linear operation of the channel and conventional MS models. In this paper, we demonstrate that an eXtremely Large (XL) Multiple-Input Multiple-Output (MIMO) system equipped with Stacked Intelligent MSs (SIM) at the RX side, together with a single antenna and its accompanying radio-frequency chain, may act as a two-layer neural network operating exclusively over the air. papers.title: Electron-photon entanglement in real space from quantum electrodynamics
papers.abs: We study the entanglement between an electron and the photon it scatters, resolved in real space and time. Starting from nonrelativistic QED in Fermi's oscillator representation, we write Fock's coupled equations for components with fixed photon number in the photon configuration space, in the length gauge, where the photon is created around the atom through a nonlocal kernel. Truncated at one photon, the equations are solved numerically without the rotating-wave approximation for a one-dimensional model atom in a waveguide with a single transverse mode and enhanced coupling. The atom is driven by a short, off-resonant laser pulse, with the electron and photon represented on real-space grids. The global electron-photon entanglement is largely transient. It peaks during the pulse and decreases as the polarized electron cloud returns to the core, leaving a state close to a product of the electron state and a superposition of the field vacuum with a single scattered photon. papers.title: Parameter-Decoupling-Informed Learning for Superresolution: Laboratory Validation and Galaxy Imaging
papers.abs: We present a parameter-decoupling-informed learning model for estimating subwavelength separations of point sources, without requiring prior knowledge of source properties, control over the sources, or continued access to their light signals. The method builds on our parameter-decoupled quantum superresolution estimation theory, which circumvents the need to estimate nuisance parameters such as partial coherence, brightness imbalance, and relative phase. Our convolutional neural network further accommodates practical imperfections, including background noise, photon loss, and centroid and orientation misalignment. We validate the method using synthetic and experimentally generated images, achieving separation-estimation fidelity above $82\%$ for separations as small as approximately $0.075σ$, where $σ$ is the Gaussian intensity-PSF standard deviation. papers.title: HarP: a simulation tool for high-order harmonic generation and propagation in gases
papers.abs: Accurately simulating high-order harmonic generation (HHG) for attosecond science requires connecting the microscopic single-atom quantum dynamics and the macroscopic propagation of intense driving laser fields. HarP is an open-source Python code designed to address this multiscale problem. It solves the wave equations for both the driving laser field and the generated harmonics, using precomputed dipole tables for the nonlinear polarization density. This tabulation enables the direct integration of accurate microscopic models while avoiding costly calculations during the propagation. The methodology builds upon the approach of [L'Huillier et al. (1992) PRA 46, 2778] and has already facilitated multiple studies on phase matching, propagation effects and HHG optimization. This paper presents the underlying physical model, its numerical implementation, and comparison against alternative simulation frameworks.

papers.title: Multimode continuous-variable quantum key distribution with CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic integration
papers.abs: Multiplexing and photonic-electronic integration offer a route to scalable and high-throughput quantum key distribution (QKD) networks through parallel transmission and compact hardware suited to volume manufacturing. Realizing this route requires multichannel transmitters and receivers, and a security analysis accounting for mode coupling. Here we present a CMOS-compatible photonic-electronic multimode continuous-variable QKD architecture, using polarization multiplexing as a two-mode example. Silicon-photonic transmitter and receiver chips prepare and detect two polarization modes in parallel. The receiver is co-integrated with a dual-channel 28-nm CMOS transimpedance amplifier, providing shot-noise clearances exceeding 20 dB in both channels. Pilot-assisted unitary digital recovery removes the need for active optical polarization control, while a multimode security analysis accounts for the mode crosstalk. At 2 percent residual crosstalk, the multimode analysis extends the simulated secure distance from 39 to 84 km, near the crosstalk-free limit of 89 km. Over 10 km of deployed fi

papers.title: Theoretical study of high-order harmonic generation in solids based on deep-learning methods
papers.abs: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids provides a compact and coherent EUV radiation, which has attracted considerable attention. Many theoretical methods for laser-crystal interactions are developed. However, an approach to treat large-scale amorphous systems with ab-initio accuracy is still lacking because of the enormous computational cost. Here, we incorporate molecular dynamics and tight-binding electron Hamiltonians based on deep-learning methods to solve the problem efficiently. Its accuracy is validated by comparing the HHG spectra of monolayer hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) with those obtained using existing methods. Then we use it to study the temperature-dependent HHG in bulk Si. We uncover a distinct harmonic-order-dependent thermal response: low-order harmonics are enhanced with increasing temperature, whereas high-order harmonics are suppressed. papers.title: Effects of Pulse Duration on Kerr Self-Focusing and Weld Formation in Ultrafast Laser Welding of Fused Silica
papers.abs: Kerr self-focusing can shift the laser interaction region away from the geometrical focus, making energy deposition near the joining interface difficult to control. Here, the effect of pulse duration on nonlinear focusing and weld formation is investigated from 262 fs to 10 ps. ICCD imaging shows clear changes in the axial position and shape of the plasma emission. Different pulse durations already produce distinct axial positions during the initial 2000 pulses, and these positions continue to evolve with pulse accumulation. The final weld morphology, weld position, and shear strength show corresponding changes. A ray-optics model including the Kerr effect is used to calculate the focal shift. The simulated trend agrees with the experiment and supports the role of Kerr self-focusing in the observed focal position change. These results clarify the relationship between pulse duration, nonlinear focusing, interaction position, and weld formation.

papers.abs: Universal fault-tolerant superconducting quantum computers are expected to require millions of physical qubits; yet extending the prevailing dedicated-control-line paradigm to this scale would exceed the wiring density and cooling-power budget of dilution refrigerators. papers.abs: In the multimode regime of cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED), light-matter coupling can be strong enough such as to allows a quantum emitter to couple with multiple resonant field modes. papers.abs: Non-invasive thermometry is highly desirable in cryogenic experiments to avoid the self-heating inherent in conventional sensors. papers.abs: Computational hyperspectral imaging reconstructs spatial-spectral information from limited optical measurements. papers.abs: We investigate native defects and their impact on the electronic structure of Td-MoTe2 and graphene/Td-MoTe2 van der Waals heterostructures using scanning tunnelling microscopy and spectroscopy. STM reveals a high density of circular, hollow surface defects that we attribute to Te vacancies. STS on pristine MoTe2 shows semimetallic, V-shaped dI/dV spectra with subtle low-energy states. The vacancies suppress the tunnelling conductance below the Fermi level without introducing new sharp defect-related resonances, consistent with a vacancy-induced redistribution of Mo-Te spectral weight rather than the appearance of new electronic states. In the heterostructure, graphene preserves these MoTe2 fingerprints with no noticeable graphene doping or charge transfer. Our results demonstrate that isolated native Te vacancies act as spectroscopically weak perturbations to the low-energy electronic structure of graphene. The graphene overlayer further screens their impact on the electronic structure, making graphene/Td-MoTe2 heterostructures intrinsically tolerant to such interface defects.

We further analyze the effect of imperfect electron preparation, showing that electron phase noise is converted into a fluctuating optical displacement and eventually limits the precision. papers.title: Electro-optic comb-driven massive data transmission on monolithically integrated lithium niobate photonic circuits
papers.abs: Driven by large AI models, the demand for datacenter interconnects is outstripping traditional scaling laws. This necessitates a transition toward dense multiplexing techniques, such as wavelength-division multiplexing (WDM), for datacenter environments, transferring long-haul spectral efficiency to short-reach, high-bandwidth applications. Integrated optical frequency combs offer compact, low-cost light sources for future datacenter WDM interconnects. However, existing Kerr comb and mode-locked laser implementations suffer from drawbacks in power efficiency, spectral flatness and phase noise. Their fixed, device-specific channel spacings often conflict with standard WDM grids, and co-integration with high-speed modulators remains challenging. Here, we overcome these limitations by demonstrating high-capacity data transmission using flat-top electro-optic combs on thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), a platform featuring flat spectra, tunable wavelengths and comb spacing, alongside native compatibility with (de-)multiplexers and high-speed modulators. papers.title: Experimental Validation of Double-Blind Fourier Holography in an HWO-Like Segmented Aperture
papers.abs: Double-Blind Fourier Holography (DBFH) is a phase-retrieval method that has been shown numerically to address wavefront-sensing challenges for future segmented-aperture space telescopes, including the Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO). DBFH uses a set of carefully selected pupil-plane amplitude masks and their corresponding focal-plane intensity measurements to construct an algebraically linear inverse problem, enabling computationally efficient and stable reconstruction of the complex pupil field. Here, we present the first experimental demonstration of DBFH using a spatial light modulator and an HWO EAC5-like segmented-aperture geometry. We reconstruct challenging pseudo-random wavefronts and compare DBFH with the established Focus-Diverse Phase Retrieval (FDPR) method. The two methods achieve comparable reconstruction precision, while exhibiting distinct strengths and limitations. We further demonstrate DBFH wavefront sensing in the presence of a binary source, a scenario that is not naturally accommodated by conventional FDPR. These results provide experimental proof of concept

papers.title: A van der Waals Floating-Gate Platform for Broadband Optoelectronic Neuromorphic Computing
papers.abs: Artificial synapses that integrate nonvolatile memory with broadband optoelectronic learning are essential for next-generation neuromorphic computing. However, their realization remains challenging because conventional floating-gate memories exhibit limited optical functionality and poor scalability. Here, we report a van der Waals ReS2/hBN/InSe floating-gate synaptic transistor that combines efficient charge storage with broadband optoelectronic learning in a single device architecture. The heterostructure incorporates InSe as a floating-gate layer for stable charge storage, hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) as a tunneling dielectric, and ReS2 as a photoresponsive channel, enabling carrier tunneling under electrical and optical stimulation. Through the combined operation of these layers, the device achieves a large memory window, an on/off current ratio exceeding 10^6, stable multilevel conductance states, and reliable retention over 10^4 s. papers.title: Synthetic staggered fields switch Neel vectors probed by magnetic resonance
papers.abs: Electrical detection of antiferromagnetic order is a critical challenge for antiferromagnetic spintronics owing to their vanishing macroscopic magnetisation. While magnetic resonance has demonstrated sub-terahertz antiferromagnetic spin pumping and nonlinear magnon dynamics, its application to electrically contacted on-chip devices has room for further exploration. Here we show that magnetic resonance enables direct electrical detection of Néel vector states. A $180^\circ$ reversal in synthetic antiferromagnets is realised by current-driven effective fields with opposite polarisation acting on each magnetic sublayer, which we term synthetic staggered fields. The switching induces a $π$ phase shift of precessional motion in time, producing hysteretic rectified voltages in our phase-sensitive detection scheme. Angular-dependent resonance analysis offers further insight into the Néel vector directions, pointing to a model beyond the macrospin formalism. We address this by defect-incorporated micromagnetic simulations that reveal fragmented domain states after current excitation. An extr

papers.title: QQLink: A Declarative Framework for Multi-QPU Quantum Workflow Orchestration
papers.abs: Distributed quantum protocols require measurement outcomes produced at one node to control operations at another. We present QQLink, a programming and orchestration layer that expresses these dependencies in a single program, using workflow nodes, deferred measurement references, and declared entanglement, and derives the cross-node coordination automatically. Its planner constructs a provably acyclic dependency graph in time linear in the total size of the instructions' qubit footprints. The same programs execute through simulator backends or are lowered to dynamic circuits on partitioned quantum hardware. We evaluate seven protocol workflows. Exhaustive feedforward-branch tests on the simulator runtime path, over tomographically complete input sets, yield output-state infidelities of at most $5\times10^{-12}$ and no incorrect classical outputs, and replaying every plan in random topological orders leaves each final state unchanged. papers.title: Interfacial Orbital Rashba Edelstein Effect Identified in CoO/Cu/Pt Trilayers
papers.abs: We investigate the generation of orbital angular momentum currents at engineered Cu-oxide interfaces using CoO/Cu/Pt thin-film trilayers. Angular-dependent magnetoresistance measurements on samples with varying Cu interlayer thickness reveal systematic changes in both longitudinal and transverse resistance components, including a sign inversion of the signal. By systematically varying the Cu interlayer thicknesses, we disentangle the spin and orbital contributions to the magnetoresistive response. Our results show that large orbital currents originate from the interfacial orbital Rashba-Edelstein effect due to the presence of the Cu-O bonds at the CoO/Cu interface. Unlike previously studied CoO/Cu bilayers that rely on uncontrolled natural oxidation, our trilayer geometry enables reproducible and stable orbital-current generation at ambient conditions. Our results identify Cu-oxide interfaces as efficient sources of orbital angular momentum and clarify the microscopic mechanism underlying orbital current generation. Consequently, this work establishes a well-defined materials platfor

papers.title: Minimal ancilla for boosting type-I photonic fusion
papers.abs: Fusion gates enable the creation of large entangled photonic states for linear-optical quantum computing and communication protocols. However, their success probability is limited to $1/2$ without additional photonic resources. Previous schemes for boosting type-I fusion have used four ancillary single photons or a two-qubit Bell state, whose preparation is probabilistic and resource intensive. Here we propose a boosted type-I fusion gate using only two independent ancillary single photons and no entangled ancillary input. It achieves a direct success probability of $5/8$, matching that of the previous four-single-photon proposal while using half as many ancillary photons. The circuit is predominantly passive, with a single active element that applies a phase shift or swaps two modes according to intermediate photodetection outcomes. Unlike the previous schemes, successful outputs occupy fixed modes and require no further conditional output routing. In particular, we show that the gate is more robust to heralded ancillary-photon loss than previously proposed boosted gates and reduces

papers.title: Yb/Sr optical clock comparison at 2.2E-18 uncertainty over a 1350-km fiber link
papers.abs: Redefining the International system of Units (SI) second requires independent frequency-ratio measurements between clocks based on different laboratories, with an overall uncertainty below 5E-18, to validate individual clock evaluations through consistency checks. Reaching this uncertainty over long distances has remained challenging. So far, comparisons at this level have been achieved only a few times, between co-located clocks, and their results disagree markedly. Previous high-precision comparisons have therefore been limited to local or kilometre-scale links. Here we compare a ytterbium optical lattice clock in Wuhan with a strontium optical lattice clock in Shanghai over a phase-stabilized fiber link spanning 1350 km, and determine the Yb/Sr frequency ratio to be 1.207 507 039 343 337 716 0(26), with a Bayesian statistical uncertainty of 1.14E-18 and a total uncertainty of 2.18E-18. papers.title: Spin and Charge Photocurrents from Electric-Magnetic Dipole Interference in Centrosymmetric Crystals
papers.abs: A common view regarding even-order nonlinear optical (NLO) effects, such as second-harmonic generation and the bulk photovoltaic effect, is that the breaking of inversion symmetry is necessary. However, this view relies on the assumption that light interacts with materials solely through its electric field. Here, we demonstrate that interference between the electric and magnetic components of the same light field can induce even-order NLO effects even in centrosymmetric materials. Using charge and spin photocurrents as prototypical examples, we present a unified microscopic theory showing how such electric-magnetic dipole interference (EMDI) drives NLO responses in inversion-symmetric crystals. Bilinear in both electric and magnetic fields, these responses scale linearly with light intensity. Combining symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations, we decompose the EMDI-induced photocurrents into shift-like and injection-like contributions and classify their dependence on crystal symmetry, time-reversal symmetry, and light polarization. Notably, we reveal that these EMDI-induc

papers.title: Axion Quasibound States in the Continuum and Their Enhanced Axion Nonlinearity
papers.abs: Dynamical axion quasiparticles (DAQs) in condensed-matter systmes have emerged as a fascinating platform for exploring axion physics and nonlinear optical phenomena. However, the amplitude of the coherent oscillating $θ$ field is even smaller than that of the static counterpart, making the experimental observation of DAQs particularly challenging. Here, we introduce symmetry-sensitive bound states in the continuum (BICs) physics to enable the all-optical detection of DAQs and enhance DAQ-mediated second-harmonic generation (SHG). Specifically, we uncover that DAQs induce optical shear that breaks the $C_{2z}$ symmetry of metagratings without geometric engineering, thereby converting symmetry-protected BICs into axion quasi-BICs (qBICs). In this context, the evolution of the quality factor and topological charge in momentum space, together with the appearance of optical resonances in far field associated with axion qBICs, offers achiral optical signatures for DAQ detection beyond the widely used Kerr and Faraday effects. Furthermore, by exploiting axion qBICs in the critical coupling

papers.title: Estimation of covariance matrix for Stokes-like measurement under phase-space deformation
papers.abs: We investigate the signatures of phase-space noncommutativity in an anisotropic oscillator and propose an optomechanical protocol to experimentally characterize it through Stokes-like measurements of an optical field. Starting from a deformed phase-space algebra characterized by the position-position and momentum-momentum noncommutativity parameters $θ$ and $η$, we employ the Darboux transformation to construct an equivalent Hamiltonian in canonical variables. The resulting effective dynamics exhibits correlations between the oscillator degrees of freedom. We derive the corresponding covariance matrix and examine how the noncommutative parameters enter the mechanical dynamics and the optical response. By coupling the oscillator to a coherent optical probe, we obtain analytical expressions for the time-dependent optical coherence attenuation and the nonlinear Kerr phase. papers.title: Functional Superoscillations in a Wave Processor
papers.abs: Physical wave processors are constrained by diffraction, but the bandwidth of the mathematical functions they implement need not be set by it. Here, we demonstrate continuous and multiplexed optical processing of superoscillatory functions, in which a scalar argument is encoded onto a wavefront and a fixed diffractive wave processor synthesizes optical responses that approximate the corresponding function outputs in parallel. Unlike conventional superoscillatory optics that generates predetermined fields, superoscillation here is expressed in the input-output dependence on the encoded argument. Its frequencies are therefore distinct from the transverse spatial frequencies of propagating light and are not subject to the same diffraction-imposed cutoff. We demonstrate complex-valued superoscillatory function synthesis and introduce a multiplexed architecture that simultaneously evaluates distinct target superoscillatory functions whose harmonic content exceeds that of the optical input encoding. Visible-light experiments further validate this beyond-encoding superoscillatory regime. To

papers.title: Nonreciprocal magneto-optic beam steering of thermal emission
papers.abs: Conventional thermal emitters obey Kirchhoff's law of thermal radiation, which ties absorptivity to emissivity and places a fundamental limit on a range of radiative energy technologies and sensing systems. This constraint can be overcome using magneto-optic materials, which exhibit nonreciprocal thermal emission under an applied magnetic field. While the spectral nonreciprocity of magneto-optic devices has been explored theoretically and experimentally, nonreciprocal control over the direction of thermal emission has received far less attention. Here, we propose and numerically demonstrate nonreciprocal beam steering of thermal emission, wherein an applied magnetic field lifts the degeneracy between guided modes at +/- kx, enabling asymmetric and tunable directional thermal emission. We highlight a III-V semiconductor photonic structure operating at 24.5 um, a wavelength with few laser sources. This structure exhibits a nonreciprocity greater than 0.5 between +/- 75 degrees at 50 mT, a peak emissivity asymmetry over 0.6 at 150 mT, and 22 degrees of beam steering between 0 and 1 T. O

papers.title: Compressive microendoscopy in the presence of noise and misalignment: the translational correlation advantage of graded-index fibers
papers.abs: Multimode fibers (MMFs) offer a minimally invasive platform for deep-tissue and multisite in vivo optical sensing. Computational microendoscopy methods extend them into the high-resolution imaging domain, but are quite sensitive to experimental errors. This study investigates the robustness of microendoscopy based on compressive sensing (CS) by comparing step-index (SI) MMFs with graded-index (GRIN) fibers. Mode-expansion-based simulations are used to assess the accuracy of image reconstruction in the presence of fundamental photon noise and lateral fiber shifts. We show that both fiber types exhibit comparable noise sensitivity, but GRIN fibers are significantly more robust to lateral misalignment errors. These results establish GRIN MMFs as an alignment-tolerant platform for robust computational microendoscopy.

papers.title: Surface Functionalization with Lasers: from Nanostructures to Applications
papers.abs: Pulsed laser sources stand out as remarkable and versatile tools in the growing interdisciplinary field of materials science, offering capabilities for tailoring and customizing materials to meet specific requirements. Their ability to induce different controlled material alterations allows enhancing material properties that might otherwise remain elusive. In essence, laser-induced material modifications encompass a spectrum of transformative processes, ranging from subtle topographical changes in the nano- and microscale, to intricate chemical modifications. Among the challenges to overcome are the creation of approaches that allow tuning the properties of light to optimize interactions on various types of solids, including metals, semiconductors, and dielectrics. Understanding these interactions is paramount towards efficiency increase of the processing techniques. This chapter embarks on a comprehensive exploration of the intricate dance between pulsed laser beams and their interaction with matter at the surface. The applications of laser-induced surface modifications are far-reac

papers.title: Non-Hermitian Topology of a Subwavelength Resonator in Synthetic Space
papers.abs: Non-Hermitian singularities and the nontrivial topology of energy bands have been extensively explored in extended periodic systems, where phenomena such as exceptional points and bulk Fermi arcs are naturally associated with periodicity and momentum space. Here, we show that this non-Hermitian topology can be extended to the domain of subwavelength resonators using a synthetic space. By reconstructing the complex energy bands of a subwavelength ring resonator in the synthetic space of geometrical parameters, we experimentally observe a spectral triplet formed by two exceptional points (EPs) connected by a bulk Fermi arc and a topologically robust quasi-bound state in the continuum (q-BIC). This Fermi-arc q-BIC emerges exactly at the intersection of the bulk Fermi arc and the q-BIC line in synthetic space, establishing a direct topological link between two spectral singularities. Encircling the EPs in synthetic space visualizes the nontrivial topology of the complex energy-band structure and reveals the opposite half-integer topological charges of the EPs connected by the bulk Fermi

papers.title: Accurate measurement of Lithium Tantalate birefringence in whispering gallery resonators
papers.abs: Lithium Tantalate (LTA) is an important ferroelectric crystal widely used in piezoelectric, electro-optic, and nonlinear optical devices. Although this crystal is very common, there is an ongoing debate regarding its birefringence magnitude, and even its sign. While some sources claim it to be negative, others maintain that it is positive. The issue is further complicated by the sample-to-sample variation in the crystal composition, ranging from congruent to stoichiometric. Here we report the experimental exploration of this question based on high-resolution spectroscopy of optical whispering gallery resonators fabricated from this crystal. These sensitive measurements unambiguously indicate that in the near-infrared range at room temperature the stoichiometric LTA is negative, while the congruent LTA is positive.

papers.title: Polarized X-rays from table-top free-electron-driven van der Waals crystals
papers.abs: Polarized X-rays are essential for polarization-sensitive techniques such as X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectroscopy, magnetic microscopy, and fluorescence imaging. These techniques are crucial in the study of molecular and material dynamics, which are in turn central to driving the global transition to clean energy and sustainability through research in photovoltaics, catalysis and optoelectronics. Currently, polarized X-rays with tunable polarization and photon energy are available only in large facilities like synchrotrons. Here, we theoretically predict and experimentally demonstrate the generation of linearly polarized X-rays from free electron-driven van der Waals crystals, without the need for additional optical stages like polarizers. We show that precise, real-time control over the polarization can be achieved by simply re-orienting the van der Waals crystal. Furthermore, we show that a high degree of polarization can be achieved across all polarization angles - from perpendicular to in-plane - with intensities exceeding 10^9 photons s^(-1) sr^(-1) mA^(-1).

papers.title: Deep-Microscopic Photonic Bandstructure of a Two-Dimensional Honeycomb Lattice
papers.abs: Conventional descriptions of light in materials rely on macroscopic models that average the optical response over the microscopic lattice structures. These models are deployed in the semi-classical limit, where the collective local response over many lattice sites is adequate. However, they fail to capture the full spatial dispersion, which requires a lattice-resolved description of light. We address this limitation by formulating a deep-microscopic nonlocal theory of the photon based on the Maxwell Hamiltonian and its characteristic equation. The solution reveals the full spatial dispersion in the form of deep-microscopic photonic bandstructure, and corresponding real-space Bloch field textures. We demonstrate our theory for a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model of a gapped honeycomb lattice. Our framework thus extends photons to the same microscopic footing as electrons or phonons, providing a unified route to studying topology, dissipation, and quantum fluctuations of light in dispersive materials.

papers.title: Polarization-resolved haze in transparent wood - towards wooden glass
papers.abs: Transparent wood (TW) composites possess residual haze that limits image clarity despite their high light transmission, yet the physical origin of this scattering has not been established. Here, polarization-resolved measurements reveal a pronounced polarization dependence of scattering by a wood-polymer composite with improved refractive index matching. Polarization- and spectrally-resolved haze as low as 21% (40-45% at 550 nm for unpolarized light) with transmittance of approximately 92% for polarization perpendicular to the fibers was detected. It is found that the low-haze spectrum closely follows an inverse-square relation over the 400-800 nm range, well described by a weak-index-contrast Rayleigh-Gans-Debye (RGD) model invoking subwavelength birefringent heterogeneities within the cell wall. This physical mechanism was previously obscured by haze-limiting strong scattering from debonding gaps or refraction at the lumen-cell wall interface. papers.title: Real Time Motion Detection in Video Inspired by Photonic Time Stretch
papers.abs: Motion perception is fundamental to computer vision and physical AI, and plays a central role in robotics, autonomous vehicles, human-computer interaction, and video compression. Traditional approaches such as background subtraction, frame-differencing and optical flow algorithms often struggle in complex or dynamic scenes, typically sacrificing spatial resolution for computational tractability. Here we introduce MoViD (Motion estimation via Virtual dispersion and phase Detection), a physics-inspired algorithm grounded in the principles that govern photonic time stretch - a highly successful ultrafast realtime data acquisition platform. Drawing inspiration from the optical physics therein, MoViD treats video as a collection of optical time series waveforms associated with pixels. Motion of an object through a pixel broadens the time series spectrum and, after group delay dispersion, induces a temporal phase that exists only if there is motion. papers.abs: We study massless scalar perturbations of rotating anti-de Sitter black strings sourced by a power-Maxwell field with negative exponent $s$. The charge enters the metric function as $-Qr^{p}$ with $p=2/(1-2s)$, and the case $s=-1/2$ gives a linear term with an algebraic horizon. Since rotation is a local boost of the static string, the rotating spectrum follows exactly from the static one evaluated at a frequency-dependent momentum. We compute the spectrum with the Horowitz-Hubeny series, Chebyshev collocation and time-domain evolution, each implemented in two independent codes and checked against the planar Schwarzschild-AdS limit. The charge acts in two ways. papers.title: Unified First-Principles Theory of Finite-Wave-Vector Photocurrents in Crystals
papers.abs: Spatially structured light carries independent phase and envelope variations in addition to its polarization and frequency. We develop a first-principles theory of second-order dc photocurrents (especially shift and injection) that resolves how these optical degrees of freedom drive distinct dc responses in crystals. The second-order dc response couples two optical field components at the same frequency but with generally different wave vectors. Expanding the response to first order in these wave vectors identifies two rank-four material tensors: $ξ$, which couples to the optical phase gradient and contains the plane-wave photon-drag limit, and $ζ$, which couples to the intensity gradient and describes a spatially varying dc current. Wannier-interpolated calculations for monolayer GeS show symmetry-allowed finite-wave-vector responses that survive at a centrosymmetric structure where conventional bulk photovoltaic effect vanishes. papers.title: Generating entanglement in quantum matter with pathway-entangled photons via resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
papers.abs: Resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS) is conventionally used to probe elementary excitations and correlations in quantum materials. Here, we propose an interferometric RIXS protocol that instead creates entanglement between spatially separated regions of a solid-state material. An incident X-ray photon is coherently split by a beam splitter into two arms illuminating opposite ends of a sample. Recombining the scattered photons at a second beam splitter and detecting an energy-selected photon then projects the material into a coherent superposition of excitations at the two ends. This protocol is the X-ray, solid-state analogue of the Duan-Lukin-Cirac-Zoller (DLCZ) heralding scheme. Using a Kramers-Heisenberg formalism with quantized photon modes, we show that orthogonal and degenerate end excitations yield maximally entangled states. We illustrate this mechanism in three models: (1) two decoupled sites yield a heralded Bell state. papers.title: On the Doppler Effect in Static Materials: Vortices and Black, White and Worm-Hole Like Wave Trajectories
papers.abs: We demonstrate the Doppler effect in a static material. The effect is achieved with a network of thin waveguides whose lengths depend on the direction of travel, chosen to simulate the compression and expansion of the wave experienced by a source travelling with velocity $v$. Each edge of length $\ell$ becomes a pair of waveguides of lengths $\ell/(1\mp v/c)$, one for each direction of travel. On a lattice this gives the field pattern of a moving source. To demonstrate the effect, we design a vortex, an analogue black hole and wormhole.

papers.abs: We demonstrate a compact single-beam optically pumped magnetometer (OPM) employing a pure 87Rb microfabricated vapor cell with 500 Torr buffer gas. We systematically characterize the OPM response as a function of laser detuning and optical intensity, and derive the magnetic-field sensitivity from the signal slope and noise amplitude spectral density. A best sensitivity of 11 fT/Hz^1/2 is achieved near the resonance transition at an optimal optical intensity, using a small cell volume of only 0.027 cm^3. Furthermore, a miniaturized OPM prototype was developed using a folded flexible printed circuit board (FPCB) to integrate the vapor cell, a compact heater, and magnetic-field coils into a cubic sensing head. Two coil configurations patterned directly on the FPCB were investigated. Under optimized operating conditions, the OPM prototype achieved a sensitivity of 66 fT/Hz^1/2. papers.abs: Quantitative phase imaging (QPI) has become a standard approach for label-free microscopy of transparent specimens, mapping the optical path length. However, the isotropic phase is blind to the molecular order underlying optical anisotropy. Implementations that also add quantitative contrast to birefringence rely on multi-frame illumination or polarization-state scanning, or on dedicated interferometric hardware and thus trade away acquisition speed or the simplicity of a standard microscope. We present Quantitative Phase and Polarimetric Imaging (QPPI), a computational imaging framework that converts a standard differential interference contrast (DIC) microscope with a polarization camera into a single-shot, video-rate, dual-contrast imaging system. We developed a new globally regularized phase reconstruction that eliminates artifacts of prior DIC-to-QPI approaches, providing quantitative phase information, and used per-pixel Stokes-based reconstruction to obtain quantitative anisotropic retardance. papers.title: Integrated elliptical III-V nanopillar arrays on silicon for dual photodetection and light emission
papers.abs: Next-generation on-chip photonic devices require compact, energy-efficient components integrating photodetection and light emission on silicon platforms. Achieving broadband photodetection combined with efficient emission in a single nanoscale device remains challenging. Here, we demonstrate elliptical nanopillar arrays monolithically integrated as III-V-on-Si templates, exhibiting broadband photoresponse across visible to near-infrared wavelengths, dynamic neuron-like graded responses under modulated light, and pronounced electroluminescence at around 865 nm under forward bias. The nanostructured elliptical geometry approach enhances optical absorption and carrier dynamics within an active area significantly smaller than commercial detectors, enabling responsivities up to 0.55 A/W at 830 nm in compact nanoarrays. This work advances the development of miniaturized active nanophotonic devices suitable for integrated sensing, emitting and communication circuits, and neuromorphic processing on silicon substrates.

papers.title: Computational imaging through turbid, bubbly and flowing water near the telescope
papers.abs: Cameras in the surf zone or behind ship wakes look through turbid, bubbly, moving water close to the lens, yet restoration networks are usually scored only on displayed images. We introduce a measured dataset of a telescope viewing displayed images and physical objects through a 25~mm water layer 45~mm in front of its objective, under seven combinations of flow, bubbles and turbidity, with clear-water recordings as a second reference. Because the suspension scatters light far outside the 1.3\textdegree{} field of view, turbidity mainly removes contrast, 4.4- to 4.8-fold on a Siemens star. Restoring the mean of eight frames improves structural similarity (SSIM) by 0.032 over a single frame, and learned fusion of the frames adds little. One raw frame supports five-category recognition (96.8\%) as well as restored images. Adding synthetic training pairs leaves display-image scores unchanged but raises the correlation of a restored Siemens star with its clear-water recording from below 0.5 to above 0.9. papers.title: Stochastic Analysis of Laser Phase Noise in Photonics-Assisted Radio Frequency Beamforming
papers.abs: This paper develops a stochastic model for quantifying the impact of laser phase noise on photonics-assisted radio frequency (RF) beamforming. Unlike conventional deterministic models, the presented theoretical framework captures the statistical randomness associated with the RF array factor of beamforming networks driven by finite-linewidth lasers. Fourier-domain analysis reveals that laser phase noise reshapes the spatial coherence function of such beamforming networks, inducing coherent RF aperture shrinkage, beam-pattern distortion, and directivity degradation. The analysis highlights that beamforming network architectures employing nanosecond-scale optical differential delays can exhibit substantial performance degradation even when driven by commercially available narrow-linewidth (kHz-range) lasers. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that average RF power gain gets downscaled and fluctuations dominate in large-aperture beamforming networks due to phase noise, imposing an upper limit on the maximum achievable RF antenna array-size. papers.abs: We study the estimation of detuning and intrinsic loss in a lossy whispering-gallery-mode (WGM) resonator located in a balanced Mach--Zehnder interferometer. We use indistinguishable photon pairs and coherent-state probes. We show that using indistinguishable photon pairs can provide higher Quantum Fisher Information (QFI) of dissipative parameters, such as intrinsic loss, at resonance away from critical coupling. Taking into account all photon-loss outcomes, we obtain analytical QFI expressions and compare photon-pair and coherent-state probe results when they have the same mean photon number. For estimating the round-trip amplitude transmission at resonance and away from critical coupling, the photon-pair probe gives a higher QFI than the coherent-state probe, and photon-number-resolved detection saturates this QFI. This advantage is due to the photon-loss statistics and it is still accessible for a typical overcoupled condition after averaging over fluctuations of the unresolved detuning. papers.title: Excitonic Stark Response Induced by Quantum Capacitance in van der Waals Heterostructures
papers.abs: Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. Here, we show that this description breaks down in the presence of interfacial charge transfer, where quantum capacitance modifies the internal electrostatics. Using interlayer excitons as local probes, we observe a dipole-dependent energy splitting that persists even when the gate-induced geometric field is nominally canceled. This splitting reflects incomplete cancellation between gate- and carrier-induced fields set by quantum capacitance, while many-body renormalization is largely symmetric with respect to the two opposite dipole orientations, allowing the splitting to provide a direct optical measure of the local chemical potential. Our results reveal the central role of quantum capacitance in interface electrostatics and provide a route to probe it in operando.

papers.title: From Hollow Waveguides to Mie Voids: Low-Index Light Confinement
papers.abs: The confinement of light within optically thin media challenges the conventional view that optical localization requires high-index dielectric materials and total internal reflection. Over the past decades, a broad range of photonic phenomena has demonstrated that electromagnetic energy can also be guided and localized inside low-index regions or nanoscale void cavities. What first appears to be a curiosity is, in fact, highly relevant: The interaction between light and matter lies at the heart of much in optics and photonics. It enables sensing, nonlinear optical phenomena, and optical manipulation, yet it also inevitably introduces absorption, dissipation, and loss. Pushing localized, enhanced, or guided energy into a lower-index space thus offers entirely new possibilities for light-matter interaction and dispersion control. In this review, we discuss some of these counterintuitive structures, starting with light guidance within optically thin media, such as hollow-core photonic crystal fibers or antiresonant reflecting optical waveguides. papers.abs: Metasurfaces are conventionally designed on periodic lattices, which renders their electromagnetic response spatially uniform and leaves the spatial arrangement itself unused as an information-bearing design resource. In this study, we propose and numerically validate a metasurface built on an aperiodic monotile: the recently discovered "hat" polykite, a single tile mathematically guaranteed to tile the plane only nonperiodically. The twelve distinguishable orientations of the hat serve as a natural design basis; each carries resonant elements tuned to one of twelve absorption frequencies between 4.600 and 4.914 GHz, transcribing the provable aperiodicity and mirror asymmetry of the geometry into the electromagnetic response. Gaussian-beam scanning over a compositionally unique 6 times 6 grid yields irregular, position-dependent electromagnetic signatures whose pairwise separations reach beyond 6 dB. papers.abs: Acoustic waves transport mechanical energy and elastic strain through solids, with material composition and shape governing their propagation. In the gigahertz hypersound regime, acoustic wavelengths reach tens to hundreds of nanometres, comparable to nanoscale device dimensions. Harnessing these waves underpins high-frequency signal processing, sensing, electromagnetic coupling and quantum control. Acoustic metrology probes elastic modes and internal interfaces. Yet directly imaging how nanoscale acoustic waves interact with local structure remains challenging, requiring picometre displacement sensitivity combined with high spatiotemporal resolution. Here we demonstrate full-field imaging of laser-induced hypersound at surfaces using reflected electron wavefronts. We introduce ultrafast low-energy electron microscopy (ULEEM), exploiting the intrinsic surface sensitivity of few-electronvolt electrons. papers.abs: State purity is a key resource for experimental tests of quantum mechanics with massive objects. Cavity cooling of a levitated nanoparticle via coherent scattering stands out as a strategy to prepare highly pure states of its roto-translational motion. In several cases, though, the performance of cooling by coherent scattering is limited by the classical fluctuations of the laser field. Here we present a quantum theory of coherent-scattering experiments which includes the effect of the laser amplitude and phase noise. We derive a master equation for the noise-averaged particle's dynamics, valid for both center-of-mass and rotational degrees of freedom, and quantify the cooling performance for different levels of noise in state-of-the-art experiments. We compute approximate analytical expressions for the laser-noise-induced heating rates and excess phonon number in both regimes of weak and strong optomechanical coupling. papers.abs: Many functionally important materials, such as silicon, possess high-symmetry crystal structures that forbid even-order nonlinear optical responses, thereby limiting their application in e.g., photonics and optoelectronics. Strain gradients can effectively break symmetries, activating otherwise forbidden optical responses. Although such flexo-photoresponses have attracted considerable interest recently, a comprehensive microscopic theoretical framework is still lacking. Here, we develop a first-principles approach that can systematically evaluate a wide range of flexo-photoresponses in realistic materials. By mapping strain gradients to long-wavelength phonons within the established theory of electron-phonon coupling, our approach captures the nonlocal quantum-mechanical effects of lattice deformations on nonlinear optical responses. papers.title: Fundamental bound on Wigner negativity generation from environmental collisions
papers.abs: Beyond quadratic potentials, classical evolution laws are typically thought to arise from quantum theory as an approximate description. Here we show that classical evolution laws can emerge exactly, provided the environment interacts with the system via collisions. We use this to derive an inequality that lower bounds the distribution of environmental momentum kicks by the absolute value of the Fourier transform of the potential. We show that violating this inequality is necessary and sufficient for a non-quadratic potential to generate negativity from the set of positive Wigner functions. A simple consequence of this is a lower bound on the heating rate for a quantum system to evolve effectively classically. We illustrate our results using the theory of a levitated nanoparticle subject to photon recoil and background gas collisions. We derive the strength of external potential needed to generate Wigner negative states in an optical tweezer and propose an experimental test of whether a nanoparticle in an optical lattice is operating in a non-classical regime.

papers.abs: The control of nonlinear optical responses in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale offers opportunities for developing two-dimensional integrated nanophotonics with programmable functionalities. In this work, we report the first realization of nanoscale nonvolatile control of the amplitude and polarization of second-harmonic generation (SHG) response in layered CuInP2S6 (CIPS) via the domain structure in an interfacial PbZr0.2Ti0.8O3 (PZT) thin film. The SHG intensity at CIPS/PZT heterointerface is continuously modulated, either substantially enhanced or almost entirely quenched, by the circular domain walls in underlying ferroelectric oxide. The interfacial coupling of CIPS polar axis with in-plane polarization of PZT domain walls tailors the SHG light polarization into two-fold (C2V) symmetry, which is well modeled by nonlinear electromagnetic theory. Overall, this study enables nonvolatile programmable design of nonlinear light intensity and polarization in van der Waals ferroelectrics at the nanoscale.

papers.abs: We develop a bosonic Bogoliubov description of Zitterbewegung in time-dependent optical-Dirac systems. Within the optical-Dirac framework, the anomalous pair-creation and pair-annihilation terms of a bosonic Bogoliubov Hamiltonian correspond to couplings between the positive- and negative-frequency sectors, whose coherence underlies the Zitterbewegung response. When the constitutive parameters vary in time, the resulting moving-frame connection generates dynamical interbranch coupling and positive--negative-frequency coherence. papers.abs: We study the material requirements for transferring the total-angular-momentum (TAM) projection of a twisted photon to the orbital angular momentum (OAM) of a photoelectron emitted from an $n$-type semiconductor surface. The OAM transfer is characterized by the mean electron OAM, its root-mean-squared width, and the fraction of electrons with OAM-projection equal to the photon TAM-projection. Efficient transfer requires the transverse momentum of the conduction electron to be much smaller than the transverse momentum width of the photon, which favors low temperatures, small conduction-band effective masses, and shallow donor levels. papers.abs: Optically bistable materials promise technological advances in optical information processing, memristive devices, and multiparametric sensing. However, optical bistability is predominantly observed under cryogenic conditions or is governed by subtle thermo-optical nonlinearities. Here, we report on Ho3+-activated nanocrystals that exhibit cavity-free intrinsic optical bistability (IOB) at ambient conditions. Non-thermal IOB stems from a cross-coupled photon avalanche (XPA) mechanism enabled by a low-phonon-energy double-perovskite host, which reduces nonradiative losses and facilitates excited-state population via XPA, even when the pump intensity is below threshold. Time-resolved luminescence measurements support the proposed XPA, as evidenced by a double-rise profile consistent with two reservoir states interlocked in energy looping. IOB with high-contrast photoswitching (up to 46 dB) is observed at room temperature across multiple visible emission lines, enabling wavelength-division multiplexing and compatibility with common detectors. papers.abs: Semiconductor triple-quantum dots (TQDs) are a promising platform for scalable quantum information processing, but the community has so far lacked access to affordable and flexible high-speed control electronics. SpinQICK, an open-source spin qubit-control package built on the Xilinx Radio Frequency System-on-Chip (RFSoC), directly addresses this gap by leveraging the high sampling-rate signal generation and advanced digital signal processing (DSP) capabilities of the Quantum Instrumentation Control Kit (QICK) to enable precise time-domain voltage control and readout of semiconductor spin qubits. In this paper, we use spinQICK to demonstrate coherent control, state preparation, and readout of a fully connected triangular exchange-only device. We also introduce and experimentally verify a novel dynamical decoupling (DD) sequence enabled by the triangular TQD and leverage its unique decoupling properties to characterize electrical noise. These results establish spinQICK as a low-cost, flexible platform for semiconductor spin qubit control and provide a pathway for hardware optimization

papers.abs: We present RADICAL, the silicon-photonic-enabled Reconfiguration-Aware Direct-Connect AI Cluster that integrates a custom spatial-and-wavelength selective switch (SWSS) with the Linux network stack. RADICAL deploys a packaged 4x4x4$λ$ microring-based SWSS into a four-GPU-server cluster using standard SFP28 optical transceivers, and a reconfiguration-aware host-networking interface to demonstrate a direct-connect reconfigurable optical fabric. The SWSS provides dynamic spatial and wavelength routing with 3.2-6.8 dB path loss, average wavelength and spatial crosstalk isolation exceeding 25 dB, and error-free 25 Gbps signal recovery across routing paths. At the system level, RADICAL validates reconfiguration-aware operation through continuous bulk data transfers totaling 6.4 TBytes over 10 minutes. We further demonstrate multitenant AI training across reconfigurable link topologies, including four ResNet-18 instances and six nanoGPT instances, with the latter sustained for more than five hours.

papers.abs: We analytically investigate the fidelity dynamics of a Jaynes--Cummings qubit coupled to a single-mode cavity in the presence of stochastic fluctuations of the qubit--cavity coupling. Such fluctuations naturally arise in cavity- and circuit-QED platforms due to fabrication imperfections, control-field noise, mechanical vibrations, and environmental disturbances. Since the qubit--cavity coupling governs the rate of coherent energy and information exchange, understanding the effects of its fluctuations is essential for assessing the performance of quantum communication, quantum sensing, and quantum information-processing protocols. We consider both Gaussian white noise and Ornstein--Uhlenbeck noise with finite correlation time as models for the coupling fluctuations. Exploiting the closed dynamics within each excitation manifold, we derive exact analytical expressions for the noise-averaged density matrix and the fidelity relative to the ideal noiseless evolution. papers.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
papers.abs: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models and spatial resolution. Here we demonstrate a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model that establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit. We discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from a pinned state directly at the channel-dielectric interface of an organic transistor, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics that contradict models based on substrate patterning. This non-destructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final configuration opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

papers.abs: We present an ultrastable laser system based on miniature core components: a self-injection-locked laser comprising a distributed-feedback laser diode and an integrated microring resonator, together with a 3-ml vacuum-gap Fabry-Perot cavity. By carefully addressing technical noise sources, in particular residual amplitude modulation, we demonstrate a thermal-noise-limited fractional frequency instability of $5\cdot10^{-15}$ for averaging times between 1 and 10 s, which is among the lowest reported for compact cavity-stabilized lasers. This performance is achieved with conventional multilayer mirrors and a moderate cavity finesse of $10^5$. Such stability of the output frequency, combined with the small size of the core components and a possibility to generate a Kerr frequency comb in the very same microring resonator, provides a path towards fully integrated photonic frequency references for transportable optical clocks and low-noise microwave synthesis.

papers.abs: The variance of bright squeezed vacuum (BSV) is not only strong but also phase dependent, yet recent strong-field experiments with BSV have recorded only its magnitude. A coherent field of the same color provides the phase reference that resolves this phase-dependent noise. Strong-field ionization of xenon by this light shows that the photoelectron yield follows the BSV quadrature along the coherent field, and that the nonlinearity of ionization amplifies the quadrature noise many times over in the electron yield. The noise is moreover distributed unevenly over the photoelectron momentum distribution, differing by an order of magnitude between ionization channels. Strong-field ionization thus offers a phase-sensitive, channel-resolved detector of quantum light, while the quadrature noise of quantum light offers a probe of the intensity dependence of individual ionization pathways.

papers.abs: In this work, we present a spatial and temporal light trapping mechanism induced by coherent frequency conversion. We consider a wave-mixing process, where a pumped nonlinearity mediates a frequency-domain beamsplitter interaction between two signal modes. papers.abs: The emergence of entangled quantum optical states in high-harmonic generation raises a fundamental problem about its characterization, namely, \textit{how can entanglement of extreme-ultraviolet radiation be certified for attosecond light fields?} Here, we provide experimentally accessible separability tests, particularly showing that attosecond photoelectron interferometry provides a direct solution to this problem. This is achieved by a quantum optical treatment of mapping photoelectron interferometry to the measurement of optical correlation functions. This yields a negative-partial-transpose witness for infrared-XUV entanglement and a sufficient witness of genuine multipartite entanglement without auxiliary optical measurements. We evaluate both witnesses on explicit optical states and identify how the protocol can be extended to XUV-XUV entanglement certification. Hence, we establish attosecond photoelectron interferometry as a general framework for entanglement certification across a wide range of optical frequencies.

papers.abs: Scientific discovery often requires identifying a small number of high-performing designs in vast, constrained search spaces. This is difficult when evaluations are costly, feasible solutions are sparse, parameters are strongly coupled, and physical constraints are strict. papers.title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
papers.abs: We review what it means for a relativistic particle to be localized and argue that the most useful approach is through local measurement. This perspective ties localization directly to relativistic causality and measurable outcomes in spacetime. Strict localization in quantum field theory is formalized by states that give the same expectation value as vacuum for all local observables outside some spacetime region. With this formalism, single photons cannot be strictly localized, but coherent states can. The structure and interpretation of local observables and local operator algebras are discussed in connection with the Reeh-Schlieder theorem. Since probabilities of local measurement outcomes cannot vanish in vacuum, particle detection events must be phrased carefully. Key characteristics of strictly localized states are surveyed alongside concrete strategies for constructing them. The relationship between localization, causality, and on-demand sources is analyzed, finding that strictly localized states can represent localized, propagating information in quantum field theory. papers.abs: Distributed Acoustic Sensing (DAS) enables dense, kilometer-scale measurements for seismic and environmental monitoring, but its performance is limited by spatially heterogeneous noise and fiber to ground coupling. Unlike traditional pairwise similarity measures, the proposed method formulates channel selection as a distance estimation problem in a coherence enhanced signal space, enabling identification of incoherent noise and coupling induced distortions without requiring prior knowledge of installation conditions or noise statistics.
